solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Some blood not English: a simple mistake?

indicators.note: not says the following letter is left out of the blood group

parts.note: type O is one group of blood, so some blood is TYPE O

explanation.surface: A medical-sounding question about a sample of non-English blood being nothing more than an error.
explanation.walkthrough: Blood group TYPE O loses its E (English, after 'not') to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A typo is a small slip made when typing or printing, the commonest kind of simple error.

clue.text: Male, warlike type, holding a chopper

indicators.note: holding says the two pieces enclose the letter A

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a hawk is a person favouring military action

explanation.surface: An aggressive man gripping an axe.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomahawk is a light axe used by Native Americans, a chopping tool.

clue.text: Painter has left it around?

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
RA, Royal Academician, is a painter

explanation.surface: Has an artist left something lying about?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' and 'around' only link here. A painter leaves behind a likeness of the sitter, so the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is a painted likeness, the kind of work a painter might leave for posterity.

clue.text: Sanction naughty boy, lip given a brief curl

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
the lip of a cup is its rim

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the word for curl loses its last letter

parts.note: a curl is a turn or twist

explanation.surface: An instruction to approve of a naughty boy whose lip gives a quick sneer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sanction' reads as a verb applied to the boy, but it is a noun meaning approval.
explanation.definitionFit: An imprimatur is an official licence or approval, originally permission from the Church to print a book.

clue.text: People eating very tiny thing

indicators.note: eating says the people swallow the word for very

parts.note: men means people
so means very, as in so good

explanation.surface: Diners are consuming something extremely small.
explanation.definitionFit: A meson is a subatomic particle, about as tiny an object as physics deals with.

clue.text: One selling farmland that can be brought back into use

definitions.text: that can be brought back into use

parts.note: a rep, sales representative, sells
arable land is farmland used for crops

explanation.surface: An agent selling fields that can be farmed again.
explanation.definitionFit: Reparable means able to be repaired, so restored to working order.

clue.text: For a change, dad's at a museum: whose?

definitions.text: For a change, dad's at a museum: whose?

indicators.note: for a change says the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dad has gone to a museum for once, and we ask whose museum it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the founder of the famous London waxworks museum, which answers 'whose?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame Tussaud founded the wax museum in London that still bears her name.

clue.text: Appreciated it's hot inside military vehicles

indicators.note: inside says the hot goes within the vehicles

parts.note: tanks are armoured military vehicles
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Soldiers welcome the heat inside their tanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying thanks is the spoken way of showing gratitude, as when someone says the favour was appreciated.

clue.text: Doing a turn in club

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the ... Club, a service organisation

explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing a turn in club' suggests a cabaret act, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotary describes circular motion, and Rotary is also the international service club.

clue.text: Heading away from capital on motorway, they get the shakes

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

indicators.note: the heading of the capital, its first letter, goes away

parts.note: Caracas is the capital of Venezuela

explanation.surface: Someone leaving a capital city along a motorway gets the jitters.
explanation.walkthrough: Caracas is the capital of Venezuela; in an across clue 'on' places a piece after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Maracas are percussion rattles that make their sound only when they are shaken.

clue.text: Hand-to-hand fighting at these crowded lodgings

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fighting at close range is fighting at these

explanation.definitionFit: Close quarters is both the short range of hand-to-hand combat and literally cramped accommodation.

clue.text: Nothing current in old transmission

indicators.note: in says the nothing and the current go inside the word for old

parts.note: past means old or former
O, the zero, means nothing
DC is direct current

explanation.surface: A dull old broadcast with no current interest.
explanation.definitionFit: A podcast is a recorded audio programme distributed online, a kind of broadcast.

clue.text: Marx discussing royalty, the main killer

parts.note: Harpo was one of the Marx Brothers
on means about or discussing
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen and so royalty

explanation.surface: A Marx brother talking about the royal family, the chief murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is the sea, so its killer hunts whales with a harpoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpooner kills whales at sea, and 'the main' is a poetic name for the ocean.

clue.text: Former scorer missing a run

indicators.note: missing says the run is taken out of the scorer

parts.note: a marker keeps the score in a game
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A one-time scorer who failed to score a single run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former' looks like 'one-time', but it means one who forms.
explanation.definitionFit: A former is someone who forms or shapes something, which is exactly what a maker does.

clue.text: A tiny piece and others covering naked back said to bring luck

indicators.note: covering says the two pieces enclose the reversed word

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount
bits are further tiny pieces, so the others

indicators.note: back says the word for naked is read the other way

parts.note: naked means bare

explanation.surface: A tiny scrap and other bits covering an exposed back, a superstitious charm.
explanation.walkthrough: BARE reversed by 'back' gives ERAB, which WHIT and BITS cover. Saying 'white rabbits' on the first day of a month is a British folk superstition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a traditional spoken charm, uttered on the first of a month for good fortune.

clue.text: Agreeing article can fit at the back, held together with string

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the can holds the string within it

parts.note: taken as written
a cord is a string

indicators.note: at the back picks the final letter of the word fit

explanation.surface: An article saying a can fits at the rear when tied with string.
explanation.definitionFit: Accordant means in accord, harmonious or in agreement with something.

clue.text: Will exercise, moving to violin

indicators.note: moving shifts the letters of the words around into a new order

explanation.surface: A will-power exercise in switching to the violin.
explanation.definitionFit: Volition is the act of using one's will to make a choice or decision.

clue.text: Superficial need to be thrown into large bin

indicators.note: into says the jumbled word goes inside the bin

parts.note: a skip is a large open waste container used in Britain on building sites

indicators.note: thrown says the letters of the word are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Shallow need for something to be chucked in the skip.
explanation.walkthrough: A skip is a British large builder's rubbish container.
explanation.definitionFit: Something skin-deep goes no further than the surface, so it is shallow or superficial.

clue.text: Gander trembled, facing his killer?

indicators.note: facing says the trembling word sits opposite, alongside, the killer

parts.note: a butcher slaughters a goose, the gander of the surface
shook means trembled

explanation.surface: A goose quakes as it faces the man who will kill it.
explanation.walkthrough: Butcher's hook is Cockney rhyming slang for look, and a gander is a look too.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang a butcher's hook rhymes with look, and to have a gander is to take a look.

clue.text: Left rival to support kind of light actor?

indicators.note: in a down clue the rival sits under, supporting, the pieces above

parts.note: UV is ultraviolet light
to vie is to compete as a rival

explanation.surface: A left-wing rival backing a lightweight actor.
explanation.walkthrough: A luvvie is British slang for a gushing, theatrical actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Luvvie is a British informal term for an effusive actor, so it is a kind of actor.

clue.text: Get excited, foothold centrally defective

indicators.note: it lacks a letter at its centre, so one middle letter goes

parts.note: a stirrup holds a rider's foot

explanation.surface: Getting worked up because a stirrup is faulty in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up is to rouse or agitate, making people excited.

clue.text: Complete eccentric forgetting name

indicators.note: forgetting says the name is dropped from the word for eccentric

parts.note: a nutter is a crazy or eccentric person

explanation.surface: A total oddball who can't remember names.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter as an adjective means complete or absolute, as in utter nonsense.

clue.text: Spending more francs in account

indicators.note: in says the francs go inside the account

parts.note: a relation is an account or narrative
F is the abbreviation for francs

explanation.surface: Extra outlay of francs is recorded in the accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflation is an economic policy of increasing spending and money supply to stimulate the economy.

clue.text: A number eating large meal

indicators.note: eating says the number swallows the large

parts.note: four is a number
L is the abbreviation for large, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Several people sitting down to a big dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meal' looks like a dinner but means ground grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Meal is coarsely ground grain, and flour is finely ground meal.

clue.text: One in bed having some lover be naked

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bedfellow with a naked lover.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'having' into the definition; it is the link joining 'One in bed' to the hidden word. The bed is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbena is a garden plant, so it is one of the flowers grown in a bed.

clue.text: Getting on with broadcast about a sort of dancing

parts.note: getting on means old, ageing

indicators.note: about says the word for broadcast is turned round

parts.note: to emit is to send out or broadcast

explanation.surface: An ageing person on air talking about a kind of dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-time dancing is the traditional ballroom style, such as waltzes and quicksteps.

clue.text: They explain poor sex: it's shattering

indicators.note: shattering breaks the letters of the words into pieces to be put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Sex therapists explain that bad sex is devastating.
explanation.definitionFit: An expositor is someone who sets out and interprets ideas or texts, an explainer.

clue.text: Trim nails back

indicators.note: back says the word for nails is read in reverse

parts.note: pins are slim nails

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut your fingernails short again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nails' suggests fingernails, but here it means pins.
explanation.definitionFit: To snip is to cut with small quick strokes of scissors, a synonym of trim.
